title: PyTorch 2.15 Speeds Mac MoE Decoding 6.5x on Apple Silicon
summary:
LFM2.5-8B-A1B inference speeds increased from 23.6 to 123.6 tokens per second on Mac hardware after the release of PyTorch 2.15. The update boosts Mixture of Experts (MoE) decoding by 5 to 6.5 times compared to version 2.14 and accelerates softmax over a 128k vocabulary by approximately 8 times. Peak driver memory for Wan2.2 VAE decoding also fell from 270 GiB to 8 GiB in the latest version.

The performance gains result from the PyTorch team at Hugging Face replacing MPSGraph paths with Metal kernels to better optimize Apple silicon. Along with these speedups, the update introduces FP8 dtype support for Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) and improves linear algebra support. The team is currently developing version 2.16 to further increase execution speeds.

selectedTweets.text:
PyTorch 2.15 is a pretty big release if you run models on a Mac.

Over the past months, the @PyTorch team at @huggingface has been working upstream on MPS, replacing MPSGraph paths with Metal kernels.

Some of the results are kind of wild:

- MoE decoding is now 5-6.5x faster than in PyTorch 2.14
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 9.4 → 61.3 tok/s on an M3 Ultra
- LFM2.5-8B-A1B: 23.6 → 123.6 tok/s
- softmax over a 128k vocab is ~8x faster
- FP8 is now supported on MPS
- Wan2.2 VAE decoding goes from ~270 GiB peak driver memory to ~8 GiB

This isn’t a specific runtime, or a separate inference engine, it’s just PyTorch getting faster on Apple silicon!

Impressive work by @Is36E! 2.16 is already looking even faster 👀

https://t.co/hzHrQbLuIK
